absent: Numeric encodings of SVM exit reasons, event injection types, interrupt control bits, TLB control values, and APIC virtualization inhibit reasons.
Full VMCB, per-CPU SVM data, per-VCPU SVM state, queued interrupt, and Xen port table layouts including sizes, offsets, and ownership.
Behavior of nested exit handling, soft interrupt RIP update, ASID allocation, AVIC completion, Hyper-V mapping and remote flush, guest memory read, and LAPIC pending set helpers.
Lifecycle and teardown of Xen event channel ports and event file contexts, and error semantics of direct event channel delivery beyond not-connected.
Conditions defining VMRUN failure, interrupt and NMI blocking, nested exit-on-event predicates, GIF and virtual GIF state, and SEV and SEV-ES guest classification.
Target CPU and statistics accounting for fail-entry reporting and injection counters.

findings.text: Xen event channel send hypercall takes a guest address holding a small port descriptor and a result slot. A guest read fault is reported as handled with a fault status. An unknown port is reported as unhandled. A known port is delivered either through a direct channel path or by signaling an associated event notifier, with success reported as handled with zero status, while a direct path failure other than not-connected is reported as unhandled.

Lookup of the Xen port identifier in the per-VM port table is done under an RCU read side critical section, while the lifetime of the found descriptor is governed by the VM source synchronization domain.
The event channel send guest descriptor has a stable width of four bytes shared by 32-bit and 64-bit guests.

SVM exit dispatch is a fixed table from exit reason to handler covering control and debug register accesses, selected exception vectors, interrupt and NMI and SMI and virtual interrupt window events, common emulated instructions and privileged operations, nested virtualization operations, EFER and control register traps, TLB and power management operations, bus lock, system management resume, AVIC fast path completions, with an extra confidential guest exit entry present only in confidential guest builds.

The observed VMCB control state used for reporting and injection includes fields for exit reason, two info words, exit interrupt info with optional error, pending event injection with optional error, next instruction pointer, TLB control, address space identifier, interrupt control with virtual NMI state, and Hyper-V enlightenment controls.
Exit and entry event reporting expose reason and info words plus interrupt information, with the accompanying error value meaningful only when both validity indicators are set and otherwise cleared.

SVM exit handling consumes nested guest exits through nested special and nested handled stages, reports hardware entry failure to userspace with reason and CPU plus diagnostics, honors fast path hints for userspace and consumed exits, and otherwise dispatches by exit reason.

Pre-run preparation detects physical CPU migration since the prior run and then invalidates address space generation, marks control state dirty, and records the new CPU; confidential guests use a separate pre-run path, otherwise a stale generation triggers allocation of a fresh address space identifier from per-CPU state.

NMI injection programs a valid NMI event; forwarding from outer to inner guest skips masking bookkeeping. Without virtual NMI, injection records software masking and arms return-from-interrupt interception. Virtual NMI pending state is queryable and can be set at most once until consumed, marks interrupt control dirty, and counts toward injection statistics in both direct and pending paths.

IRQ injection distinguishes soft from external interrupts, may first adjust soft interrupt return state and be consumed there, releases a previously armed AVIC window inhibit when no further injectable interrupt remains or when nested execution is active, then records tracing and statistics and programs the pending event from vector plus validity and type.

APIC virtualization IRQ window requests are reference counted. The operation is inert when virtualization is disabled. When unrelated inhibit reasons are already present it takes a read lock and only adjusts the window count, deferring the actual inhibit change. Otherwise it takes a write lock and changes the actual inhibit only on transitions between zero and one requester.

Nested return address fixup applies only with nested execution active and a nested run pending. It synchronizes the next instruction pointer with the current instruction pointer when hardware supports next pointer reporting but that support is hidden from the outer guest, and refreshes saved soft interrupt address metadata when a soft interrupt injection is outstanding.

LAPIC interrupt delivery records the vector in the pending interrupt set and then orders that update against the guest mode check before completing virtualized delivery, so either entry observes the new request or a doorbell is raised after entry.

Control register intercept for task priority is never changed for encrypted-state guests nor when nested task priority virtualization applies. Otherwise it is cleared by default, left cleared when no interrupt is pending, and re-armed when current priority meets or exceeds the highest pending interrupt priority.
Nested task priority virtualization is active exactly when executing an inner guest whose nested interrupt controls request interrupt masking virtualization.

NMI and IRQ allow checks distinguish three outcomes: blocked, busy, and allowed. Busy covers a pending nested run and injection into an inner guest when the corresponding event should instead exit to the outer guest; blocked covers architectural masking or interrupt blocking; otherwise injection is allowed.
NMI masking uses hardware blocking state when virtual NMI is enabled and software masking plus return-from-interrupt interception otherwise.

IRQ window enabling requires global interrupt flag or virtualized flag support. With virtualized APIC enabled outside nested execution it arms a per-CPU window flag once and increments the VM-wide window request count, then arms the virtual interrupt notification.

NMI window enabling relies on a pending return-from-interrupt exit when NMIs are masked, returns immediately for encrypted-state guests that signal readiness separately, relies on a start-interrupt exit when global interrupts are disabled, and otherwise single steps with trap and resume flags after saving prior flags.

Current address space TLB invalidation first purges Hyper-V flush state, then uses a hardware per-address-space flush when available and otherwise forces a fresh identifier by retiring the generation. The current-root variant additionally flushes nested mappings through Hyper-V when enlightened nested TLB is active with a valid root. The all-CPU variant expects enlightened remote flushes to use a separate remote path. The guest variant also marks a register dirty before invalidating.

Single address invalidation uses a direct address plus identifier invalidation only for shadow paging; with nested paging it performs a guest-wide invalidation and optionally reports to the caller that the operation covered the full scope.

Address space generation wraparound is explicitly unresolved. A single identifier is assumed to cover outer and inner guests with nested transitions providing the needed invalidation. Reaching the generic all-CPU flush while enlightened remote flush is active indicates a bug or a failed remote flush and triggers a warn plus recovery attempt. Direct address invalidation is avoided with nested paging due to reported hardware errata and guest instability.

Requesting an NMI window while virtual NMI masking is active is unexpected and warned. Encrypted-state guests cannot be single stepped for NMI unblocking and must keep control register intercepts cleared with traps used instead. The generic SVM instruction wrapper converts an instruction fault into a spurious fault report rather than propagating the fault.
Exit reason and interrupt information are 32-bit quantities while the two companion info values are 64-bit quantities in the exit and entry reporting interfaces.
